title: Clear L vs Dark L Allophony
objectives: Distinguish clear alveolar /l/ and dark velarized /ɫ/
Produce dark L in coda position and before consonants

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Clear L vs Dark L Allophony. Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner uses clear L at the end of "feel".
💡 Solution: Raise back of tongue toward throat while saying /l/ to produce dark [ɫ].

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Clear L vs Dark L Allophony
1. Definition: The phoneme /l/ has two major positional variants (allophones) in English.

2. Rule: 1. Clear L [l]: Tongue tip touches alveolar ridge before a vowel (leave, light, play). 2. Dark L [ɫ]: Back of tongue raises toward velum (velarization) at the end of a syllable or before a consonant (full, milk, ball, little).
3. Why? Position in syllable structure triggers secondary velar articulation at syllable codas.
4. How to recognize? Check if L precedes a vowel (Clear) or comes at coda/before consonant (Dark).
5. Common examples: Clear L: leave /liːv/, light /laɪt/, play /pleɪ/; Dark L: full /fʊɫ/, milk /mɪɫk/, ball /bɔːɫ/, little /ˈlɪtəɫ/
6. Counter-examples: Irish/Welsh accents which use Clear L in all positions.
7. Exceptions: Clear L retained when adding vowel suffix (ball -> balling = Clear L).
8. Common mistakes: Replacing Dark L with /w/ (*miwk for milk) or using Clear L at word end.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: L before vowel = Clear & Light! L at end of word = Dark & Deep!
10. Key vocabulary: clear L, dark L, allophony, velarization, syllable coda, approximant
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🔵 B2
13. Associated Visual: 👅 Tongue tip touch (Clear L) vs Tongue back rise (Dark L).
14. Key Takeaway: L before vowel = Clear! L at end/before consonant = Dark /ɫ/!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Where is "clear L" used? (Before vowels, like "light" and "play")
CCQ 2: Where is "dark L" used? (At the end of syllables or before consonants, like "ball" and "milk")
CCQ 3: What part of the tongue raises for dark L? (The back of the tongue toward the velum)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Classify as Clear L or Dark L:
🎯 Item: leaf ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Clear L (before vowel)
🎯 Item: feel ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Dark L (syllable coda)
🎯 Item: milk ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Dark L (before consonant)
